issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int, but the solution implements a static method named computeMealCost(Meal) instead. Additionally, the (commented) Main calls calculateTotalPrice as an instance method (shop.calculateTotalPrice(...)), which conflicts with the requirement that the method be static. This naming/signature mismatch between specification, solution, and Main will confuse students about the expected API and may cause tests expecting calculateTotalPrice to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution's computeMealCost(Meal) method to calculateTotalPrice(Meal) and ensure it is static (or add a static calculateTotalPrice wrapper delegating to computeMealCost). Also update any callers (e.g., Main) to call the static calculateTotalPrice method consistently to match the problem specification and UML.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) requires a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int, but the code uses a differently named method computeMealCost(Meal) in SealSaloon. Template Main also references computeMealCost, whereas the solution Main calls calculateTotalPrice. This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual operation (compute/calculate the total price of a meal) creates confusion for students mapping the requirement to the implementation and may cause compilation/test failures due to the mismatched method name.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name for this operation. Rename computeMealCost(Meal) in SealSaloon to calculateTotalPrice(Meal) (and make it static as required by the UML), and update all calls (in Main and any other files) to call calculateTotalPrice. Alternatively, if computeMealCost is preferred, update the problem statement/UML to reference computeMealCost instead.
